hero.badge: For growing businesses with operational complexity
hero.headline: Growth shouldn't make your business <highlight>harder to run</highlight>.
hero.subhead:
Carlsson Studio helps growing businesses replace spreadsheets, disconnected tools, and manual workflows with production-ready software built around how they actually operate.



Built through real operational challenges.

Designed for businesses that have outgrown manual workflows.

symptoms.title: Does this sound familiar?
symptoms.intro: Operational problems rarely announce themselves. They show up as small frictions that get heavier with every branch you open.

items.1: Each branch has drifted into its own way of working
items.2: Reports arrive after the decision has already been made
items.3: Stock in the system rarely matches stock on the shelf
items.4: Someone still merges Excel files by hand every month
items.5: Managers wait on you to approve routine decisions
items.6: Customers get a different experience at each location
items.7: Every new branch makes operations harder, not easier
items.8: The business can't run a full week without you in it

symptoms.closing: If several of these look familiar, the constraint usually isn't effort. It's that the work has outgrown the way it's organised.

outcomes.title: From operational chaos to operational clarity.
outcomes.intro: What changes when the way you operate is designed rather than improvised.

1.title: Less manual work
1.body: Data is entered once and flows where it's needed, instead of being re-typed into three places.

2.title: One standard across branches
2.body: The same process everywhere, whether you run two locations or twenty.

3.title: Visibility while it still matters
3.body: See sales, stock and performance as they happen — not when the month closes.

4.title: Less dependence on the owner
4.body: Routine decisions follow rules your team can apply without waiting for you.

5.title: One source of business data
5.body: Sales, inventory, staff and customers in one place that agrees with itself.

6.title: Decisions based on facts
6.body: Numbers you can act on, instead of estimates assembled by hand the night before.

industries.title: Built for operationally complex businesses.
industries.intro: Our strongest experience is with businesses that run real operations — multiple locations, physical stock, schedules and staff on shift. We work outside these industries too; this is simply where we've done the most.

whyCustom.title: Not every business problem should be solved with custom software.
whyCustom.intro: Plenty of operations run perfectly well on tools they already own. Building something custom adds cost and responsibility, so it should only happen when there is a reason it can't be avoided.
whyCustom.conditionsTitle: Custom software is usually worth it when:

1.title: Off-the-shelf tools no longer fit
1.body: You've started working around your software instead of with it — exports, side spreadsheets, rules that live in someone's head.

2.title: Operations have become fragmented
2.body: The same information is entered in several places, and no two of them agree by the end of the week.

3.title: Several departments need one source of truth
3.body: Sales, stock, finance and operations are each right in their own system, which means the business has no single answer.

4.title: Scaling is creating operational complexity
4.body: Every new branch, product line or shift pattern adds coordination work that no existing tool absorbs.

whyCustom.closing1: Our job isn't to sell software.
whyCustom.closing2: Our job is to recommend the right operational solution.

projectsFail.title: Why many software projects fail.
projectsFail.intro: Most failed systems were built competently. They failed earlier than the code — in what was decided before anyone started building.

1.avoid: We map how the work runs today before proposing anything to build.

2.avoid: A process that doesn't work gets fixed first. Automating it only makes the problem faster.

3.mistake: Choosing technology before defining the business goal
3.avoid: The goal is agreed first. The stack is chosen afterwards, to serve it.

4.mistake: Treating software as the solution instead of operations
4.avoid: The system is one part of the answer. Roles, rules and handovers are designed alongside it.

approach.title: How we work.
approach.intro: Seven steps, each there to remove a specific risk before it becomes expensive.

1.title: Understand operations
1.why: So the system is designed around how your business actually earns money — not around a feature list.

2.title: Map the current workflow
2.why: Writing down how the work runs today exposes the steps, exceptions and manual fixes nobody thinks to mention.

3.title: Design a better workflow
3.why: The improvement is agreed on paper first, where changing your mind costs a conversation instead of a rebuild.

4.title: Prototype
4.why: You see and use the workflow before it's built, so misunderstandings surface while they're still cheap to fix.

5.title: Develop
5.why: Built in working increments on proven foundations, so progress is visible instead of promised.

6.title: Deploy
6.why: Real data, real users, a planned cutover — your team is trained before the old way is switched off.

7.title: Continuous improvement
7.why: Operations keep changing. The system is adjusted as they do, instead of slowly drifting out of use.

fit.title: Who we work best with.
fit.intro: Being honest about this early saves both sides a great deal of time.
fit.goodTitle: We are usually the right partner if:

good.2: You manage multiple teams or locations
good.3: Manual work is slowing your growth
good.4: Existing software doesn't fit how you actually work
good.5: You want an operational system for the long term

fit.badTitle: We may not be the best fit if:

bad.1: You only need a landing page
bad.2: You only need a company profile website
bad.3: A ready-made SaaS product already solves your problem

fit.closing: If the second list describes you, we'll say so — and point you somewhere more useful.

mission.headline: Software should fit the business — not the other way around.
mission.body: Carlsson Studio builds custom business systems for founders and operators who have outgrown spreadsheets, disconnected tools, and manual workflows. Every system starts from how your team actually works — and ships production-ready, end-to-end, with one person accountable for the whole stack.

technology.title: Technology
technology.description: Proven, boring-in-a-good-way technology — chosen for reliability and long-term maintainability, not hype.

1.q: How long does a project take?
1.a: Most foundation-based projects ship in 6–10 weeks. Starting from a production-tested system removes months of groundwork — the timeline is spent on your workflows, not on rebuilding login screens.

2.a: Yes. You receive the source code, the deployment, and the documentation. No lock-in, no license fees on your own software.

3.q: My industry isn't listed. Can you still help?
3.a: Very likely. The foundations share a library of reusable modules — authentication, roles, dashboards, reporting, payments — that recombine into systems for any business domain.

4.a: Fixed-scope proposals. After discovery you get a written proposal with the recommended foundation, the customizations, the timeline, and the price — before any commitment.

5.q: Who maintains the system after launch?
5.a: We do, if you want us to. Every project includes a handover period, and ongoing maintenance and feature development are available as a retainer.

6.q: Where does Carlsson Studio work from?
6.a: An independent software studio based in Indonesia, working remotely with founders and operators across Southeast Asia.
